hints.content: We can use the distance the simulated biker has traveled to figure out how far Julian has traveled. Then we can find his average speed.

The simulated biker has traveled $20\,\dfrac{\text{km}}{\text{h}}$ for $15$ minutes. There are $60$ minutes in $1$ hour.

$\begin{align}
\text{distance}&=\text{speed}\times \text{time}\\\\
&=20\,\dfrac{\text{km}}{\text{h}} \times 15\,\text{min}\\\\
&=20\,\dfrac{\text{km}}{\cancel{\text{h}}} \times 15\,\cancel{\text{min}}\times \dfrac{1\,\cancel{\text{h}}}{60\,\cancel{\text{min}}}\\\\
&=\dfrac{300}{60}\,\text{km}\\\\
&=5\,\text{km}
\end{align}$

The simulated biker has traveled $5\,\text{km}$.

Julian's position is $-2\dfrac{1}{4}$, which means he has traveled $2\dfrac{1}{4}\,\text{km}$ less than the simulated biker has.

$5-2\dfrac{1}{4}=2\dfrac{3}{4}$

Julian has traveled $2\dfrac{3}{4}\,\text{km}$.
Julian has had an average speed of $11\dfrac{\text{km}}{\text{h}}$ so far.

question.content:
Julian is using a biking app that compares his position to a simulated biker traveling Julian's target speed. When Julian is behind the simulated biker, he has a negative position.

Julian sets the simulated biker to a speed of $20\,\dfrac{\text{km}}{\text{h}}$. After he rides his bike for $15$ minutes, Julian's app reports a position of $-2\dfrac{1}{4}\,\text{km}$. 

**What has Julian's average speed been so far?**


[[☃ numeric-input 1]] $\dfrac{\text{km}}{\text{h}}$

options.labelText: average speed in kilometers per hour
